messages:
Priya: FYI I ran a sampling job on staging and found a strong correlation between evicted-prefetches and sudden tenant bursts. Thinking out loud: instead of soft-pins with TTL, what about changing eviction scoring so entries carry an 'origin' tag (prefetch|access|pin) and a dynamic bias that decays over time.

Dan: Interesting. So prefetch entries would start with score_penalty=+X (makes them cheaper to evict) but that penalty decays over T seconds. If an access happens we remove the penalty immediately.

Omar: That would avoid immediately evicting entries that transition from prefetch->real use. Also avoids extra state machine for soft vs hard entries. Simpler to reason about in eviction comparator.

Tess: Two risks: 1) read-after-write correctness if a prefetch returns stale data after a write, 2) complexity in telemetry because we now need to attribute misses/evicts to origin + decay state. We should add a test harness that replays write-heavy traces.

Priya: Agreed on tests. For (1) we can keep a small generation check: prefetch entries include a prefix-gen at time-of-fill; any subsequent write increments prefix-gen and invalidates older prefetches. That's similar to current tombstone checks.

Dan: Implementation sketch: in ResidencyEntry { origin: enum, origin_ts: secs, bias: float } Evict comparator uses base_score + origin_bias(now-origin_ts). origin_bias for prefetch = -B*exp(-k*dt). access origin_bias = 0. pinned origin_bias = +Inf.

Omar: Either exponential or linear decay works. Exponential gives tail but needs tuning. Suggest default B=0.7 (70% cheaper) and half-life 2s. We can make config knobs.

infra-bot: sampling metrics pasted:
```
prefetch_origin_percent: 18%
evict_of_prefetch_within_1s: 34%
post_prefetch_hit_rate_1s: 22%
```

Tess: 34% evicted within 1s is high. But if 22% of prefetched entries get used, the decay approach could salvage that 22% while still reclaiming others. Need cost model: wasted GPU cycles vs latency saved for hits.

Priya: Experiment plan: 1) implement origin tag + bias (config off by default). 2) Canary in staging with traffic replay for 12h, measure: eviction_churn, post_prefetch_hit_rate, p50/p95 for misses. 3) If post_prefetch_hit_rate up and churn down -> small prod canary. 4) rollback if eviction_churn increases > 1.5x or p95 increases > 10%.

Dan: Also add a metric `evict_score_delta` to track how much bias changed eviction ordering vs baseline. That helps debug tuning.

Omar: Unit tests: simulate sequences: miss->prefetch->evict, miss->prefetch->access (should promote), write->prefetch invalidation. Add property tests that eviction comparator is stable and deterministic.

Tess: We should also consider multi-tenant fairness: an origin bias could let aggressive tenants' prefetches occupy slots longer. Maybe add an origin_bias cap per-tenant (max additional residency allowed).

Priya: Good catch. We'll add per-tenant soft-budget: origin_bias only applies if tenant_residency < tenant_budget_threshold. Otherwise bias=0. That keeps fairness.

infra-bot: Proposed rollout flags:
```
--evict.origin_bias.enabled=true
--evict.origin_bias.base=0.7
--evict.origin_bias.half_life_secs=2
--evict.origin_bias.tenant_budget_pct=0.05
```

Priya: I'll own the PR for the eviction comparator changes. Dan will add metrics and config. Omar will add tests. Tess will own the experiment doc + fairness validation.

Dan: I'll start a small perf run locally and post numbers. Priya lmk if you want help debugging sorter determinism.

Priya: Thanks team. If staging looks ok we'll iterate on B and half-life. Plan to have a canary next week. :rocket:
